grade_of_content: G3 (Sep 2025-Apr 2026 blocks of the G4 workbook), G1-3 Value Ed, G2/G3 ICT, ungraded contests/soil
note: Held back by orchestrator ruling: not G4 activities. Kept for the G3 auditor.

rows.unit: Unit 3 – Poems from around the world
rows.name: Write a short poem about thunder
steps: Read the poems Dancing Poinciana, Hurricane and The thunder is a great dragon and talk about the sounds and pictures in them.
List words that sound like thunder and storms.
Write a short poem about thunder using some of the listed words.
Read the poem to a partner.

levels.0: Poem is not started or is a single plain sentence with no describing words.
levels.1: Writes a few lines about thunder with help finding words from the shared word list.
levels.2: Writes a short poem about thunder that uses sound words and at least one picture in words.
levels.3: Writes a thunder poem with a chosen rhyme or rhythm and explains which words create the storm sound.

rows.note: Unit 3 text and writing tasks come from the cell; steps 1-2 and 4 are plain sequencing around them. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.unit: Unit 3 – Poems from around the world
rows.name: Write a haiku
steps: Read the Cat haiku and clap the syllables of each line.
Notice the pattern of three short lines.
Choose a subject from nature and note words for it.
Write a haiku of three lines and share it aloud.

levels.0: No haiku written, or lines run on without a three-line shape.
levels.1: Writes three lines with help counting syllables, one line may be too long or short.
levels.2: Writes a three-line haiku with the syllable pattern kept in each line.
levels.3: Writes a haiku and then rewrites one line to give a clearer picture, saying why the new line is better.

rows.note: Syllable pattern 5-7-5 is common knowledge, not stated in the cell; cell names 'Write a haiku' and 'Cat haiku'. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.unit: Unit 3 – Poems from around the world
rows.name: Perform a favourite poem for others
steps: Choose a favourite poem from the unit and read it three times.
Practise with voice changes and gestures.
Perform the poem to a group or the class.
Discuss one feature of the poem with the audience.

levels.0: Poem is read in a low voice or not performed.
levels.1: Performs the poem reading from the page, with prompting on expression.
levels.2: Performs the poem clearly with voice changes for the mood of each line.
levels.3: Performs from memory with gestures, and explains one feature such as rhyme or repeated words.

rows.note: Cell lists 'Perform a poem to others', 'Perform a favourite poem' and 'Discuss the features of the poem'. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Write a storyboard for a new version of a myth
steps: Read the myths Bear and Fire and Mulan and note what is the same and what is different in retellings.
Choose one myth and decide what to change.
Draw a storyboard of the new version in boxes with a line of text under each.
Share the storyboard with a partner.

levels.0: Storyboard has one box or events are out of order.
levels.1: Fills a storyboard with the main events with help sequencing the boxes.
levels.2: Storyboard shows a new version of the myth in order with a line of writing under each box.
levels.3: Storyboard changes the setting or an event and the writer explains how the change alters the ending.

rows.note: Cell names the task; steps are sequencing around it. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Role play characters from a myth
steps: Listen to a myth read aloud.
Choose a character and talk about what that character says and does.
Act out a scene of the myth in a group.
Discuss the similarities and differences between myths and legends.

levels.0: Does not take a part in the scene.
levels.1: Takes a part with prompts about what to say and do.
levels.2: Acts a character with words and actions that match the myth.
levels.3: Acts a character and explains how the myth and a legend they heard differ.

rows.note: Cell lists perform a story in a group, role play characters from a myth, discuss similarities and differences. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Write a letter, an email and a postcard
steps: Read Arturo's email, Mrs Sabella's postcard and Mrs Sabella's letter of complaint.
Talk about when to use a formal and an informal letter.
Label the parts of a letter on a sample.
Write a letter or email to a person, using the right parts and tone.

levels.0: Writing has no recognisable letter parts.
levels.1: Writes a letter with help placing the greeting and closing.
levels.2: Writes a letter with the parts in order and a tone that suits the reader.
levels.3: Writes both a formal and an informal version and explains what changed.

rows.note: Unit 5 outline is in cells A27 and A33. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Rewrite a story as a play script
steps: Read Four Clever Brothers (Parts 1, 2 and 3).
Look at the layout of a play script: names, stage directions, dialogue.
Rewrite one part of the story as a play script.
Write further dialogue for a scene and act it out.

levels.0: Story text is copied without any script layout.
levels.1: Writes a few lines in script layout with help placing names and stage directions.
levels.2: Rewrites one part of the story as a script with names, directions and dialogue in the right layout.
levels.3: Writes extra dialogue that fits the characters and acts it out for the class.

rows.note: Cell lists the writing and speaking tasks of Unit 6. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Write an adventure story with a character portrait
steps: Read the play script Out in the Forest and Dragon Boy parts 1 and 2.
Write a character portrait of the main character.
Make a book cover for the story.
Write a three-paragraph adventure story and share it.
rows.materials: Dragon Boy, Out in the Forest

levels.0: Story is a few unconnected sentences.
levels.1: Writes an adventure story with help planning the three paragraphs.
levels.2: Writes a three-paragraph story with a character described and a clear beginning, middle and end.
levels.3: Story uses similes or personification and the writer explains the effect of one of them.

rows.note: Writing tasks are named in the Feb cell. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Write an information text and a class holiday guide
steps: Read the Holiday facts file and the texts on Australia and the Neotropics.
Talk about features of non-fiction such as headings and facts.
Write an information text on a chosen place.
Make a class holiday guide with the texts.

levels.0: Text is not about a place or has no facts.
levels.1: Writes a few facts about a place with help from the model text.
levels.2: Writes an information text with a heading and facts that are true.
levels.3: Separates facts from opinions in the text and adds a contents page to the class guide.

rows.note: Unit 8 tasks are named in the cell. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Write a poem and perform it (limerick or shape poem)
steps: Read the poems Wednesday, Whether the Weather and There Was an Old Man With a Beard.
Talk about what makes the poems funny and how they are built.
Write a limerick or a shape poem of your own.
Perform your poem for others.

levels.0: Poem is not written or not shared.
levels.1: Writes a poem with help finding rhymes.
levels.2: Writes a poem in a chosen form with rhymes that fit and reads it aloud.
levels.3: Performs the poem and explains the feature of its form such as rhyme scheme or shape.

rows.note: Unit 9 tasks named in the cell. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Dicey fractions project
steps: Roll dice to make fractions of a whole.
Record each fraction as a number and in a drawing.
Compare and order the fractions made.
Share the findings with the class.

levels.0: Fractions are not recorded or parts are unequal.
levels.1: Records fractions of a whole with help from a fraction strip.
levels.2: Shows each fraction as equal parts of a whole and writes it correctly.
levels.3: Orders the rolled fractions on a number line and explains how two of them compare.

rows.note: Cell names the project 'Dicey fractions (Fractions)'; steps are from the name and unit, not a plan. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Venn variety project
steps: Choose two features to sort a group of objects or the class.
Draw two overlapping circles.
Place each object where it belongs and count each section.
Explain what the overlap shows.

levels.0: Items are not sorted into the diagram.
levels.1: Sorts most items into a Venn diagram with help placing the overlap.
levels.2: Sorts items into a two-circle Venn diagram and reads the counts.
levels.3: Builds a Venn diagram for a question they chose and draws one conclusion from the counts.

rows.note: Cell lists '#Project - G3- Venn variety'; steps from the name. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Chance experiment
steps: Use the words certain, likely, unlikely and impossible for events.
Run a chance experiment such as picking from a bag.
Record the results in a tally.
Describe the results using chance words.

levels.1: Records results with help and uses one chance word.
levels.2: Records results in a tally and describes events with chance words.
levels.3: Predicts the next result with a reason and explains why a result differs from the prediction.

rows.note: Cell: Use the correct language when describing chance events; Do chance experiment, show and describe the result. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Estimate and measure the mass of objects
steps: Pick an object and estimate its mass.
Weigh it on a scale or balance.
Compare the estimate with the measurement.
Use fractions of a unit to describe the mass.

levels.1: Weighs an object with help reading the scale.
levels.2: Estimates and then measures the mass and says how close the estimate was.
levels.3: Orders several objects by mass and describes one mass using a fraction of a kilogram.

rows.note: Cell: estimate and measure the objects; use measurement that measures mass; fraction when describing mass. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Find lines of symmetry and reflect a shape
steps: Fold a paper shape to find a line of symmetry.
Find horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry in 2D shapes.
Sketch the reflection of a shape.
Check with a mirror.

levels.0: Cannot show a line of symmetry.
levels.1: Finds a line of symmetry on some shapes with help folding.
levels.2: Finds horizontal and vertical lines of symmetry and sketches a reflection.
levels.3: Checks reflections with a mirror and finds shapes with more than one line of symmetry.

rows.note: Cell: find horizontal and vertical line of symmetry; sketch the reflection of a 2D shape. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.unit: अक़ल का पुरस्कार / सारी दुनिया मेरी है
rows.name: Letter writing (पत्र लेखन)
steps: Read the poem 'सारी दुनिया मेरी है'.
Talk about the parts of a letter.
Write a letter about the poem to a friend.
Read the letter aloud.

levels.1: Writes a few lines of the letter with help with the greeting.
levels.2: Writes a letter in Hindi with greeting, body and closing.
levels.3: Writes a letter that responds to the poem's idea with a reason.

rows.note: Cell lists पत्र लेखन under सारी दुनिया मेरी है; steps from the name. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Map and photo frame activity (मान चित्र, फोटो फ्रेम)
steps: Read the poem and talk about the world and the places in it.
Draw a map (मान चित्र) of the places in the poem.
Make a photo frame with a drawing and a line of writing.
Display the frames.

levels.1: Makes a map or frame with help adding places or words.
levels.2: Makes a map and a frame that match the poem with a line of Hindi writing.
levels.3: Explains in Hindi how the map or frame shows the poem's idea.

rows.note: Cell lists मान चित्र, फोटो फ्रेम, कविता लेखन; steps are from these names. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Slogan and scrapbook (नारा, स्क्रैपबुक)
steps: Read the poem 'कुछ कर दिखाएँगे'.
Write a slogan (नारा) about doing your best.
Collect pictures and words for a scrapbook page.
Write a sentence under each picture and share the page.

levels.0: Page has pictures but no writing.
levels.1: Writes a short slogan with help from a model.
levels.2: Writes a slogan and sentences that go with the pictures.
levels.3: Presents the scrapbook page and explains why the slogan fits the poem.

rows.note: Cell: नारा, स्क्रैपबुक, वाक्य लेखन गतिविधि. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Chart paper activity and advertisement (चार्ट पेपर, विज्ञापन)
steps: Read the story 'ऐसे मिली सज़ा' or the conversation on rivers.
Collect information and rivers' names on a chart paper.
Draw a picture and describe it in sentences.
Make an advertisement and tell the class how people respond.

levels.0: Chart is blank or has no Hindi writing.
levels.1: Adds a few labels and words with help.
levels.2: Makes a chart with information from the text and presents it in Hindi.
levels.3: Adds an advertisement and gives a reason for each claim in it.

rows.note: Cell: चार्ट पेपर गतिविधि, जानकारी, चर्चा, नदियों के नाम, चित्र-वर्णन, विज्ञापन. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Information board activity (सूचना बोर्ड)
steps: Read the text 'क्या सीखा आपने'.
Pick the facts to share.
Make an information board with a picture and notes.
Present the board in Hindi.

levels.1: Adds picture and a few words with help.
levels.2: Makes a board with a picture and facts and presents it.
levels.3: Answers a classmate's question about the board in Hindi.

rows.note: Cell: चित्र-निर्माण, सूचना बोर्ड गतिविधि, चर्चा. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Hindi dictation and reading routine (श्रुतलेखन, पठन)
steps: Listen as the educator reads words or a line.
Write what was heard (श्रुतलेखन).
Check spellings with the educator.
Read a short passage aloud.

levels.1: Writes most words with several errors, corrects some after checking.
levels.2: Writes the dictated words and line with correct letters.
levels.3: Writes a longer dictated passage and corrects own errors.

rows.note: Cell: Routines for Hindi class: श्रुतलेखन (dictation), पठण (reading). Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Nest-making and poem reading (घोंसला बनाने की गतिविधि)
steps: Read the poem 'चिड़िया का गीत' and notice the birds' sounds.
Make a nest from craft materials.
Read the poem aloud and give it a new title.
Write a line for the poem.

levels.1: Reads the poem with help on some words.
levels.2: Reads the poem aloud and writes a new title.
levels.3: Writes a new line for the poem and explains the choice of title.

rows.note: Cell: कविता-वाचन और नया शीर्षक, घोंसला बनाने की गतिविधि, कविता-लेखन. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Separate mixtures: dissolving and filtering
steps: Sort materials into solids, liquids and gases.
Try dissolving different materials in water.
Filter a mixture through paper.
Record which materials dissolve and which separate.

levels.1: Filters a mixture with help setting up the filter.
levels.2: Filters a mixture and records what dissolved and what did not.
levels.3: Predicts which materials will dissolve and tests the prediction.

rows.note: Cell lists 2.1 solids liquids gases, 2.2 separating mixtures, 2.3 Dissolving, 2.4 Filtering, 2.5 separating materials from rocks. A G3 unit. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Shadows and transparent, translucent materials
steps: Make a shadow with a torch and an object.
Change the shadow by moving the object or light.
Test which materials let light through: transparent and translucent.
Record the results in a table.

levels.1: Tests materials with help and sorts some of them.
levels.2: Tests and sorts materials by how much light passes through.
levels.3: Explains how the shadow changes with the position of the light.

rows.note: Cell lists 3.1 Shadows, 3.2 Changing shadows, 3.3 Transparent and Translucent materials. G3 unit. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Life Cycle project
steps: Choose an animal and find out its life stages.
Draw each stage in order.
Label the stages.
Present the life cycle to the class.

levels.0: Stages are missing or out of order.
levels.1: Draws the stages with help ordering and labelling.
levels.2: Shows the stages in order with correct labels.
levels.3: Compares two life cycles and explains one difference.

rows.note: Cell: #Project- Life Cycle. Steps from the name. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Food chains
steps: Group animals by what they eat.
Build a food chain from a plant.
Draw arrows to show who eats what.
Explain the chain to a partner.

levels.1: Builds a chain with help with the arrow direction.
levels.2: Builds a food chain with the arrows pointing to the eater.
levels.3: Builds two chains that join and explains what happens if one animal is removed.

rows.note: Cell: Animal group and different life cycles, Food chains. Steps from names. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Micro:bit input and output programs
steps: Connect the micro:bit and display your name.
Write a program using an input such as a button.
Make it show an output such as a message.
Test and fix it.

levels.1: Program runs after help with connecting and blocks.
levels.2: Program takes a button input and gives an output.
levels.3: Adds a loop or a second input and explains the program.

rows.note: Cell: Understand micro:bit basics, Develop input/output programs, Apply loops, Debugging. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Spreadsheet with formulas
steps: Open a sample data set.
Type the data in a spreadsheet.
Add a formula to total a column.
Make a chart from the data.

levels.1: Enters data with help with the formula.
levels.2: Enters data and uses a formula to total a column.
levels.3: Chooses a chart and explains what the data shows.

rows.note: Cell: Analyze sample data sets, Create spreadsheets with formulas. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Create your own Smart Bedroom
steps: Learn how robots and sensors help in homes.
Plan a smart bedroom with inputs and outputs.
Build the project on the computer.
Present the smart bedroom.

levels.1: Plans one smart item with help.
levels.2: Plans and builds a smart bedroom with inputs and outputs.
levels.3: Explains how a human and the machine share the work in the room.

rows.note: Cell: Project: Create your own Smart Bedroom. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Paper strip weaving and cardboard loom
steps: Learn the over-under weaving pattern with paper strips.
Make a cardboard loom.
Weave yarn on the loom.
Join the weaving into a classroom weaving wall.

levels.1: Weaves a few rows with help keeping over-under.
levels.2: Weaves with a clear over-under pattern on paper and loom.
levels.3: Weaves a pattern of their own and adds it to the wall.

rows.note: Cell: Paper strip weaving, Make a cardboard loom, Classroom weaving wall project. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Paper plate bowl weaving
steps: Prepare a paper plate with slits.
Weave strips through it.
Shape it into a bowl.
Display the bowls.

levels.0: Weaving is loose or not attached.
levels.1: Weaves with help keeping the strips tight.
levels.2: Weaves a bowl with strips held in place.
levels.3: Weaves a pattern with colours and explains why it is eco-friendly.

rows.note: Cell: Paper plate bowl weaving - Eco-friendly weaving. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Grain to flour and ladoo; pickles and papads
steps: Learn where flour comes from.
Make flour the traditional way.
Make ladoo.
Talk about preservatives and make pickles and papads.

levels.0: Does not take part in the steps.
levels.1: Takes part with help from the educator.
levels.2: Follows the steps and describes where flour comes from.
levels.3: Explains how a preservative helps the pickle last.

rows.note: Cell: Grain to Flour: From Wheat to Ladoo; Talking About Preservatives; Making of pickles and papads. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Steam in a pan and baking observation
steps: Observe water turn to steam in a pan with the educator.
Observe dough change when baked.
Talk about texture, colour, smell and taste before and after.
Discuss safety rules.

levels.1: Shares one observation with help.
levels.2: Describes how the dough or water changes with heat.
levels.3: Explains steam in daily life such as cooking rice.

rows.note: Cell has numbered steps: 1 Observe raw dough changes; 2 Talk about texture etc.; 3 Understand heat; steam in pan 1-4. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Nail string art and Samaaroh decor stitching
steps: Plan a pattern.
Wrap coloured string around nails to make it.
Use stitching to make decor for Samaaroh.
Show the work.

levels.1: Wraps string to make part of a pattern with help.
levels.2: Makes a pattern with string around nails.
levels.3: Designs a decor piece and explains the choices.

rows.note: Cell: Nail String Art - create patterns by wrapping colourful strings around nails; Samaaroh Project. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Physical features of India
steps: Look at a map of India.
Find mountain ranges, plateaus, plains and deserts.
Mark them on an outline map.
Share one fact.

levels.1: Finds some with help.
levels.2: Marks mountains, plateaus, plains and deserts on a map.
levels.3: Explains how two features differ.

rows.note: Cell: Physical Features of India — Understand mountain ranges, plateaus, plains, deserts. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: India map: 28 states and capitals
steps: Look at the India map.
Learn the states.
Place each state and capital on an outline map.
Check with a partner.

levels.1: Marks a few with help.
levels.2: Marks states and capitals on the map.
levels.3: Names states in a region and their capitals from memory.

rows.note: Cell: India Map - 28 states and its capital city. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Transportation through time
steps: Find out how people travelled long ago.
Order the ways on a timeline.
Talk about how transport changed work and life.
Present the timeline.

levels.1: Orders a few with help.
levels.2: Orders transport on a timeline and says how it changed.
levels.3: Explains one effect on society.

rows.note: Cell: Trace the development of transportation methods; Understand the impact. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Studying artworks of Paul Klee and Yayoi Kusama
steps: Look at artworks by the two artists.
Talk about lines, colours and patterns.
Make an artwork inspired by one artist.
Share your artwork.

levels.1: Makes an artwork with help choosing a pattern.
levels.2: Makes an artwork inspired by an artist.
levels.3: Explains what was taken from the artist.

rows.note: Cell: Studying artworks of Paul Klee and Yayoi Kusama. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Henri Rousseau jungle texture drawing
steps: Look at Henri Rousseau's jungle paintings.
Practise texture by shading.
Draw a jungle with leaves.
Share the drawing.

levels.1: Shades some parts with help.
levels.2: Draws a jungle with different textures by shading.
levels.3: Explains how layers create depth.

rows.note: Cell: Texture Drawing through shading; Artist Focus Henri Rousseau Jungle. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Paper sculpture and clay work
steps: Learn paper techniques such as folding.
Make a paper sculpture.
Shape clay or dough.
Add your piece to a portfolio.

levels.1: Makes a simple form with help.
levels.2: Makes a paper sculpture and a clay form.
levels.3: Explains how structure holds the shape.

rows.note: Cell: Paper Sculpture; Clay and Dough Work; Portfolio Building. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

rows.name: Keyboard and basic notes (music)
steps: Learn the seven basic notes on the keyboard.
Practise a few alankars.
Practise the Republic Day song.
Play for the class.

levels.1: Finds the notes with help.
levels.2: Plays the seven notes in order.
levels.3: Plays an alankar from memory.

rows.note: Cell: Keyboard introduction. Playing basic seven notes; Practise different Alankar. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.

steps: Revise basic karate stances.
Practise body position.
Practise basic movements slowly.
Hold stances with balance.

levels.2: Holds the stance steady with correct position.
levels.3: Moves between stances keeping balance.

Practise punching on command.
Revise kicks with knee lift.
Kick at low targets with control.

levels.1: Strikes with help on form.

Practise punch-punch-kick combinations.
Practise a basic kata.
Keep a strong stance.

rows.note: Cell: Basic Blocks; Combination Training; Katas. Added by the CP-54 auditor pass.
